name: Shankarabharanam
arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3 S
avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
notes: Same notes as the Western major scale but sung with Carnatic gamakas; expansive and majestic

name: Kalyani
arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3 S
avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 R2 S
notes: Uses the sharp prati madhyamam (M2) which gives it a bright auspicious glow

name: Kharaharapriya
arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
notes: Warm and compassionate; lends itself to long slow exploration

name: Thodi
arohana: S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S
notes: Heavy oscillating gamakas; considered one of the most demanding raagas; primarily devotional and grand with deep longing; dramatic especially in upper-octave (tara sthayi) sancharas

name: Mayamalavagowla
arohana: S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N3 S
avarohana: S N3 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
notes: The first raaga most students learn (sarali varisais)

name: Natabhairavi
arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
notes: Comforting and contemplative with gentle devotion; same notes as the Western natural minor scale

name: Keeravani
arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N3 S
avarohana: S N3 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
notes: Same notes as the Western harmonic minor; yearning quality

name: Charukesi
arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D1 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G3 R2 S
notes: Tender with a touch of pathos

name: Shanmukhapriya
arohana: S R2 G2 M2 P D1 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D1 P M2 G2 R2 S
notes: Intense and dramatic with devotional yearning; often associated with Lord Murugan

name: Shubhapantuvarali
arohana: S R1 G2 M2 P D1 N3 S
avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G2 R1 S
notes: Deep pathos and dramatic longing; R1 G2 M2 D1 N3 intervals create acute tension

name: Lathangi
arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D1 N3 S
avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G3 R2 S
notes: Sharp prati madhyamam paired with D1 and N3 creates poignant dramatic tension

name: Mohanam
arohana: S R2 G3 P D2 S
avarohana: S D2 P G3 R2 S
notes: Five-note (pentatonic) scale; Bhoop in Hindustani; bright and immediately likeable

name: Hamsadhwani
arohana: S R2 G3 P N3 S
avarohana: S N3 P G3 R2 S
notes: Pentatonic; a favourite for concert openers and Ganesha krithis

name: Hindolam
arohana: S G2 M1 D1 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D1 M1 G2 S
notes: Pentatonic; Malkauns in Hindustani; meditative

name: Abhogi
arohana: S R2 G2 M1 D2 S
avarohana: S D2 M1 G2 R2 S
notes: Pentatonic; gentle and devotional. Karnatik.com also lists an alternate scale with P: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 S

name: Revati
arohana: S R1 M1 P N2 S
avarohana: S N2 P M1 R1 S
notes: Pentatonic; ascetic and contemplative

name: Madhyamavati
arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
avarohana: S N2 P M1 R2 S
notes: Pentatonic; traditionally sung at the end of a concert (mangalam) as it is considered auspicious

name: Sri
arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
avarohana: S N2 P D2 N2 P M1 R2 G2 R2 S
notes: Auspicious; one of the ghana raagas

name: Bilahari
arohana: S R2 G3 P D2 S
avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
notes: Ascends like Mohanam and descends like Shankarabharanam; sparkling and cheerful. Karnatik.com notes N2 as a bhashanga (foreign) note

name: Nattai
arohana: S R3 G3 M1 P D3 N3 S
avarohana: S N3 P M1 R3 S
notes: Vigorous; often used to open concerts; first of the Pancharatna krithis. Parent undisputed (R3 G3 M1 P D3 N3)

name: Arabhi
arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
notes: Brisk and bold

name: Saveri
arohana: S R1 M1 P D1 S
avarohana: S N3 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
notes: Plaintive devotion

name: Vasantha
arohana: S M1 G3 M1 D1 N3 S
avarohana: S N3 D1 M1 G3 R1 S
notes: Name means spring; fresh and pleasant. Parent split: D1 (Tyagaraja/modern) points to 15 and D2 (Dikshitar/variant) to 17. Karnatik.com uses the D2 form under 17 Suryakantam

name: Kambhoji
arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 S
avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
foreign_notes: N3 (in the phrase S N3 P D2 S)
notes: Majestic; one of the great expansive raagas

name: Neelambari
arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 P N3 S
avarohana: S N3 P M1 G3 R2 G3 S
notes: Classic lullaby raaga

name: Anandabhairavi
arohana: S G2 R2 G2 M1 P D2 P S
avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
notes: Tender and soothing; used in lullabies and folk-flavoured songs. Parent split comes from heavy use of bhashanga D2 over native D1. Karnatik.com gives the arohana as S G2 R2 G2 M1 P D2 P N2 S and lists several alternate scales

name: Begada
arohana: S G3 R2 G3 M1 P D2 P S
avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
notes: Bright and energising with a majestic assertive streak. Karnatik.com gives the arohana as S G3 R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2 D2 P S

name: Kapi
arohana: S R2 M1 P N3 S
avarohana: S N2 D2 N2 P M1 G2 R2 S
notes: Lyrical and emotive; popular for lighter pieces late in a concert

name: Sindhubhairavi
arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S
scale_note: approximate - freely uses many foreign notes; arohana frequently starts on lower N2 (N2 S R2 G2 M1...)
notes: Flexible and emotional; very popular for bhajans and closing pieces. Parent split comes from R1 vs R2 emphasis in opening phrases. Karnatik.com places it under 10 Natakapriya

name: Abheri
arohana: S G2 M1 P N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
notes: Comforting and soothing with nostalgia. Not the same as Karnataka Devagandhari: modern Abheri uses D2 while Karnataka Devagandhari uses D1. Karnatik.com lists Dikshitar's Veenabheri under 20 Natabhairavi with D1

name: Khamas
arohana: S M1 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
notes: Light and playful; popular for javalis and tillanas. Karnatik.com gives a straight scale: S G3 M1 P D2 N2 S / S N2 D2 P M1 G3 S

name: Kanada
arohana: S R2 G2 M1 D2 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 P M1 G2 M1 R2 S
notes: Graceful and rich

name: Kadanakuthuhalam
arohana: S R2 M1 D2 N3 G3 P S
avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
notes: Zig-zag ascent gives it a sprightly bouncy character

name: Bhairavi
arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
scale_note: bhashanga; arohana also sung S G2 R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S (both accepted)
notes: One of the oldest and weightiest raagas; D2 in ascent and D1 in descent

name: Chakravakam
arohana: S R1 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R1 S
notes: Ahir Bhairav in Hindustani is a close cousin

name: Nalinakanthi
arohana: S G3 R2 M1 P N3 S
avarohana: S N3 P M1 G3 R2 S
notes: Short lilting raaga; very popular for lighter krithis

name: Hamsanadam
arohana: S R2 M2 P D3 N3 S
avarohana: S N3 D3 P M2 R2 S
scale_note: D3 often omitted in modern lighter pieces (S R2 M2 P N3 S / S N3 P M2 R2 S); Venkatamakhin's asampurna version includes D3
notes: Bright and luminous; prati madhyamam with no gandharam

name: Bowli
arohana: S R1 G3 P D1 S
avarohana: S N3 D1 P G3 R1 S
notes: Listed by Karnatik.com as an early-morning raaga (before sunrise), with Bhupalam. Added at the owner's request with Sriman Narayana.

name: Bhupalam
arohana: S R1 G2 P D1 S
avarohana: S D1 P G2 R1 S
notes: Parent: 8 Hanumatodi (owner decision; some references give 45 Shubhapantuvarali). Karnatik.com lists it as an early-morning raaga.

name: Malayamarutham
arohana: S R1 G3 P D2 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D2 P G3 R1 S
notes: Often confused with Valaji, which has the same scale without R1 (Karnatik.com). Time of day not given on the trusted sources.

name: Ritigowla
arohana: S G2 R2 G2 M1 N2 D2 M1 N2 N2 S
avarohana: S N2 D2 M1 G2 M1 P M1 G2 R2 S
notes: Moods from: devotional_reflective (inferred from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reetigowla, found by the curator agent, confirmed by the curator, raaga-level); compassion (curator); contemplation (curator); Added via ManoRaga proposal #6 on 2026-11-22 (sources checked by the agent; approved by curator)

name: Yamunakalyani
arohana: S R2 G3 P M2 G3 P D2 N3 D2 S
avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 M1 R2 S
notes: Moods from: devotional_reflective (inferred from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamunakalyani, found by the curator agent, confirmed by the curator, raaga-level); romantic_nostalgic (curator); grand_uplifted (curator); tranquility (curator); Added via ManoRaga proposal #7 on 2026-11-22 (sources checked by the agent; approved by curator)
